title: Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996 — Section 25 (Default of a party)

content.overview: Unless otherwise agreed, if the claimant fails to communicate the statement of claim, the tribunal shall terminate the proceedings; if the respondent fails to communicate the statement of defence, the tribunal shall continue without treating that failure as an admission of the claimant's allegations; if a party fails to appear at a hearing or to produce documentary evidence, the tribunal may continue and make the award on the evidence before it.
content.glance: Claimant default → terminate; respondent default → continue without treating as admission; non-appearance/non-production → continue and award on available evidence.
content.study: Section 25 is subject to party agreement. Claimant default on the claim leads to termination. Respondent default on the defence does not amount to admission. Non-appearance or non-production allows continuation and an award on the evidence before the tribunal.

sections.heading: Claimant default
sections.body: Failure to communicate statement of claim → termination of proceedings.

sections.heading: Respondent default
sections.body: Failure to communicate statement of defence → continue; not an admission of allegations.

sections.heading: Non-appearance or non-production
sections.body: Tribunal may continue and award on the evidence before it.

examples.title: Application of aca-s-25
examples.body: Facts that satisfy the elements stated in the provision produce the consequence described in the text.

hypotheticals.question: Do the facts engage aca-s-25?
hypotheticals.analysis: Compare the facts with the statutory elements stated in the text.

distinctions.title: Scope of aca-s-25
distinctions.body: Applies only within the elements and consequences stated in the statutory text.

misconceptions.myth: aca-s-25 creates unlimited or extra-statutory rights.
misconceptions.correction: It operates only as stated in the provision.

questionsAndAnswers.question: Does failure to file a defence equal admission under section 25?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: No. The tribunal shall continue the proceedings without treating that failure as an admission of the allegations of fact made by the claimant.

examTips: Distinguish claimant termination from respondent non-admission.

enhancement.definition: Section 25 specifies consequences of party default in arbitral proceedings.
enhancement.legalPrinciple: Claimant default terminates; respondent default is not admission; non-appearance allows award on available evidence.

shortAnswer.prompt: What is the core rule under section 25?
shortAnswer.answer: Claimant default → terminate; respondent default → continue without admission; non-appearance → award on available evidence.

tenMark.point: State the consequence of claimant default on the statement of claim
tenMark.application: Tribunal shall terminate the proceedings unless otherwise agreed.

tenMark.point: State the consequence of respondent default on the defence
tenMark.application: Tribunal shall continue; failure is not treated as admission of the claimant's allegations.

tenMark.point: State the rule on failure to appear or produce evidence
tenMark.application: Tribunal may continue and make the award on the evidence before it.

tenMark.point: Note that the rules are subject to party agreement
tenMark.application: Section 25 opens with 'unless otherwise agreed by the parties'.

sixteenMark.point: Explain the asymmetric treatment of claimant and respondent default
sixteenMark.application: Termination for missing claim; continuation without deemed admission for missing defence.

sixteenMark.point: Apply section 25 to a non-appearing respondent
sixteenMark.application: Continue and decide on the evidence; do not treat silence as admission.
